subject: MATHEMATICS
applicability_conditions: learner must expand a squared binomial in algebra or coordinate geometry
use when distance/equidistance modelling is correct but expansion fails
anchor: A binomial square is a repeated product: (a-b)^2=(a-b)(a-b); the middle term comes from two cross-products.
ordinary_language_bridge: Squaring a difference does not mean squaring each term separately; both factors contribute two cross-products.
reconstruction_route: rewrite the square as a repeated product
multiply each term in the first factor by each term in the second

minimal_contrast.prediction_prompt: Which expansion contains every product from (x-3)(x-3)?

misconception_discriminator.probe: ask for the uncompressed product line before any formula is used
misconception_discriminator.decisive_response: learner generates both cross-products and the correct sign

repair_route: ban immediate formula recall for one cycle
return to formula only after reconstruction succeeds
verification_method: substitute a simple numerical value into both original and expanded forms
compare symbolic expansion with repeated multiplication
known_limitations: does not repair unrelated equality transformations
does not cover higher-degree binomial powers
